output.summary: The district accepts $4,100 from the Tulare County Office of Education to support the district's College and Career Pathway coordinator taking part in the 2025-26 Leadership Development Institute. The grant period is July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, and began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies $15,000 for BRAVE Bay Area to teach human trafficking prevention to secondary students

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $15,000.00

output.summary: BRAVE Bay Area, an Oakland nonprofit, is a partner in a human trafficking youth prevention grant program. It will train district staff, teach the Protect Curriculum to students at two secondary schools, and host monthly workshops for caregivers. The agreement ran July 1 through September 30, 2025, and the board is ratifying it after it ended.

output.headline: Accepts $1.94M from the state for the Opportunity Young Adult Career Pathway Program through March 2027

money.evidence: accepting $1,940,425.83

output.summary: The district accepts $1,940,425.83 from the State of California Employment Development Department, which passes the funds through, to support the Opportunity Young Adult Career Pathway Program run by the Adult and Career Education office. The grant runs April 1, 2025 through March 31, 2027, and began before this vote.

vendor.name: State of California, Employment Development Department

output.headline: Adds $60,000 for Aurora Environmental's mold, lead and chemical testing at schools

money.evidence: in the additional amount of $60,000.00

output.summary: The board adds $60,000 to the contract with Aurora Environmental Services, raising it from $99,000 to $159,000. The company does a required science chemical survey, tests air for mold at school sites and buildings, and helps with water testing for lead. The term stays July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.

output.headline: Pays Kingmakers of Oakland up to $10,000 for an early reading program at MLK/Lafayette Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00

output.summary: The district approves an agreement with Kingmakers of Oakland to create the Jegna Journey Program, an early education reading program, at MLK/Lafayette Elementary School. The agreement runs August 11, 2025 through May 28, 2026 and costs no more than $10,000, paid from a grant. The board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Pays Destiny Arts Center up to $10,000 for weekly dance and music classes at Madison Park Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00

output.summary: The district approves an agreement with Destiny Arts Center to teach weekly dance and music classes to students at Madison Park Academy - Lower Campus. The agreement runs September 2, 2025 through May 30, 2026 and costs no more than $10,000, paid from Title I low-income grant funds. The board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Pays Hazard, Young, Attea & Associates up to $150,000 to run the search for a new superintendent

money.evidence: at a cost not to exceed $150,000.00

output.summary: The district approves an agreement with Hazard, Young, Attea & Associates (HYA), an executive search firm, to conduct the search for the next Superintendent of Schools. The agreement runs November 13, 2025 to November 13, 2026 and costs no more than $150,000 from the General Fund. It was negotiated under an earlier board resolution and a request for proposals.

output.headline: Moves $4,452.72 at Fremont High from teacher stipends to conference expenses
output.summary: The board approves a change to Fremont High School's 2025-2026 plan and budget funded by Measures N and H. It lowers the teacher stipend line from $41,562.50 to $37,109.78 and raises the conference expenses line from $3,240 to $7,692.72. The change moves money within the school's plan and adds no new spending.

output.headline: Moves $1,631.19 at Bunche Academy from teacher stipends to a part-time counselor position
output.summary: The board approves a change to Ralph J. Bunche Academy's 2025-2026 plan and budget funded by Measures N and H. It lowers the teacher stipend line from $9,323.60 to $7,692.41 and raises the counselor salary line, which pays for a counselor at one-tenth of a full-time position, to $15,391.17. The change moves money within the school's plan and adds no new spending.

output.headline: Shifts $35,625 at Skyline High from administrator and coach salaries to teacher stipends
output.summary: The board approves a change to Skyline High School's 2025-2026 plan and budget funded by Measures N and H. It lowers the line for supervisor, administrator and instructional coach salaries from $183,606.62 to $147,981.62 and creates a $35,625 teacher stipend line. The change moves money within the school's plan and adds no new spending.

output.headline: Shifts $70,000 at Skyline High from administrator and coach salaries to substitute teachers
output.summary: The board approves a second change to Skyline High School's 2025-2026 plan and budget funded by Measures N and H. It lowers the line for supervisor, administrator and instructional coach salaries from $147,981.62 to $77,981.62 and raises the teacher substitutes line from $19,695.67 to $89,695.67. The change moves money within the school's plan and adds no new spending.

output.headline: Confirms the board president's pick of a community member for the school bond oversight committee
output.summary: The board confirms the Board President's appointment of a Community at Large Member to the Independent Citizens' School Facilities Bond Oversight Committee for Measures A, B and J. The appointment takes effect November 13, 2025 and fills a term that ends June 30, 2027. The item has no stated cost.

output.headline: Approves Measure G1 carryover funding requests for named schools from the 2024-25 school year
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution approving requests to carry over unspent 2024-2025 Measure G1 funds for named schools, as recommended by the Measure G1 oversight commission. The official text does not list the schools or dollar amounts.
